summary: Two ordinarily proportioned human subjects stand beside each other. One uses her left hand to hold an open catalogue above a two-person card transfer, with right and left grips respectively on opposite card edges. The viewpoint must show the complete transfer beneath the public screen.

body_ownership.reason: The woman owns the catalogue-supporting left hand and the upper card-gripping right hand. The guest owns the lower card-gripping left hand and his separate catalogue hand. Distinct wrists prevent merging.
prompt_evidence: her right thumb and index finger hold the upper edge
the guest's left thumb and index finger take its lower edge

joint_chain_and_reach.reason: Both people stand close to one shared waist-level catalogue. Arms reach forward within ordinary elbow range; no cross-body or behind-back reach is required.
prompt_evidence: Her left hand holds the open catalogue level at her waist
the hands approach from opposite sides

support_and_balance.reason: Standing upright with natural weight through the legs is plausible. The light open catalogue is borne by the woman left hand and the guest stabilizes a page without supporting her body.
prompt_evidence: He keeps his other hand on the visible catalogue page

contact_and_space.reason: The catalogue is above the two transfer hands and the same card lies between opposite edge grips. The card and hands use the visible vertical gap rather than occupying the page plane.
prompt_evidence: a shallow horizontal roof over their lower hands
The same single card bridges both grips

visibility_and_projection.reason: A three-quarter-length guest-side view includes the face, waist-level catalogue, separate wrists and card. Their shared focal region and near placement make all endpoints visible at once. The catalogue hides the exchange from the room, not from the capture camera.
prompt_evidence: The folded card and joined transfer are visible to the camera from the guest side
both faces, the catalogue and the card-transfer hands in one readable focal region
